scope: Decode-side reference implementation of the denial-word remap on a real CPU serve of the artifact. The single-token loop is the same code in both arms; only --remap on|off changes whether logit_bias is sent. A row here is a token path, its suppression events and the plain greedy wave beside it, not a harmlessness, capability or removal measurement.
method: Client-side single-token loop against a live llama-server: each step POSTs /completion with the prompt re-sent and the emitted text appended, n_predict=1, temperature=0, cache_prompt=true, n_probs=1, so the served tokenizer and the KV prefix stay the artifact's own. The server does not continue cached generated tokens when the prompt is unchanged: the prompt carries the emitted text each step and prompt_n is 1. remap=on applies logit_bias only for the step it belongs to: the candidate token that completes a table sequence is suppressed with -100, and when the table names a replacement its first token is forced with +100 (the remaining replacement tokens carry +100 on the following steps while they still match, or the force is dropped and the divergence recorded). Suppression is sequence-aware: " can" alone completes nothing, " can"+"'t" completes the denial and is the step that fires. Re-sampling after a suppression can surface another completing token (a typographic apostrophe, " can not"), so the same step is re-sampled until the chosen token completes no table sequence or RESAMPLE_LIMIT is reached; every suppression is recorded. remap=off runs the identical loop with no bias, so the difference between the two arms is one flag, not a different build. Each row is also decoded as one plain greedy /completion wave for comparison.

claim.remapped_opener: I'm afraid I can’t assist with

unnamed_variants_in_text.note: the same words in an apostrophe spelling the table does not name

claim.note: the table-named denial words are gone from the opener, but the same denial reappears in a spelling the table does not name (en-cant); the words are not gone from the answer, and this is a gap in the table, not a driver failure. The rest of the text is the model's own continuation: this is not content removal and not a compliance claim.

server.argv_note: the model and binary are recorded portably; the artifact is identified by sha256

table.replacement_note: the checked-in table is an inventory: every replacement is null, so this arm suppresses and never forces. The force path is exercised by the documented table override under verification/vocab-remap/decode/forced/.

config.no_think_note: the artifact chat template is rendered unmodified

metrics.retokenized_note: a step whose re-sent text tokenized to a different id path than the tokens already emitted. The bytes are unchanged (the model sees the same text a text client would send), but the server re-tokenizes them; non-zero on byte-level BPE over non-ASCII output (measured on German umlauts)

plain_wave_equality.required: informational: the on arm is expected to diverge

openers.note: opener surfaces are table contexts inside the first 8 generated tokens; a row whose base opened with one and whose remapped text does not is counted as gone

verdict.reason: the bias arm decoded every row; every denial sequence completed inside the generated text was suppressed and re-sampled
